traits.native_range: Casuarina equisetifolia, SE Asia/Australia/Pacific beaches (widely naturalised), needle-like branchlets, 6-35 m — Wikipe
traits.leaf_shape: needles or scale leaves, evergreen (larch deciduous)
traits.trunk: single straight trunk, whorled branches, conical crown
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

leaf.note: true leaves are whorls of minute scale teeth; the drooping needle-like green branchlets are drawn as needles

bark.note: grey-brown, rough, furrowed and flaking in vertical strips on old trunks; smooth when young

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two small green cotyledons, then a thread-like stem bearing whorls of tiny toothed scale leaves on jointed green twigs, like a horsetail. Grows 1-3 m a year as a narrow pine-like cone with a straight leader and drooping needle-like branchlets, only later opening into an irregular wispy crown.
growth.source: PROSEA (early growth >3 m/yr, >10 m at 10 yr, lifespan 40-50 yr, epigeal germination within 2 weeks, no pretreatment, seedlings fail in the shade of Casuarina stands); Parrotta 1993 USDA SO-ITF-SM-46 (flowering from 2-3 yr)

fruiting.source: PROSEA Casuarina equisetifolia (male spikes 7-40 mm at twig tips, female heads grow into woody cone-like infructescences 10-24 x 9-13 mm, wind-pollinated, cones mature 18-20 weeks after flowering, valves open to release samaras 6-8 mm); Parrotta 1993 (two flowering peaks)

canopy.silhouette: flat-topped umbrella on a leaning red-plated trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with 6-9 cotyledons and bluish, finely toothed single primary needles through the first year or so, then long (15-25 cm), stout, grey-green paired needles. Young trees grow fast into open cones with thick, orange-brown, deeply fissured bark developing early; cones cluster in whorls on the branches.
growth.source: Wikipedia (fast-growing hard pine, 20-35 m; dense natural regeneration; cones 8-22 cm, green then glossy red-brown at 24 months, opening slowly over years or after fire); growth curve, first cones and lifespan estimated from Atlantic maritime-pine forestry

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (cones conic, 8-22 cm long and 4-6 cm wide, green, ripening glossy red-brown when 24 months old, then opening slowly over years or after being heated by fire); spring pollination; crop and decay estimated

bark.note: long creeping stems, green flushed purple-red, rooting at the nodes

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two broad, deeply notched, butterfly-shaped cotyledons, then thick, glossy, two-lobed 'goat's-foot' leaves on a trailing stem. The seedling runs straight out over the sand as a cord-like runner that roots at the nodes and branches, spreading many metres into a net of runners and leathery leaves across the upper beach and foredune.
growth.source: SANBI PlantZAfrica (flowers pink-violet, open one morning, bees main pollinators, capsule 12-17 mm, seeds need scarification); ANPSA (flowers 20-25 mm wide, last one day, any time of year, fast spreading); Wikipedia (runners several m, rarely 30 m, floating hairy seeds). Plant lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: SANBI PlantZAfrica (funnel flowers 30-60 mm long, pink to violet, one-day, bees plus butterflies and moths, spherical capsule 12-17 mm with 4 floating hairy seeds); ANPSA (flowers year-round in the tropics). Fruit set, ripening, hang, rot and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two narrow strap-like cotyledons, then small long-stalked, rounded, waxy blue-grey leaves with soft marginal teeth lying flat on the sand while a thick taproot plunges deep (to metres). Over 2-3 years the rosette of stiff, leathery, spiny-edged glaucous leaves grows larger before the first branched flowering stem.
growth.source: Useful Temperate Plants (germinates in 5-90 days at 20 C; very long taproot, resents disturbance); Isermann & Rooney 2014, Biological Flora of the British Isles: Eryngium maritimum (J. Ecol.); Wikipedia (flowers Jun-Sep, 1.5-2.5 cm heads). Ages estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Big seeds in corky, floating pod segments sprout in the drift line (in spring on Atlantic coasts, after autumn rains in the Mediterranean). ground.silhouette: silvery hairy grass tufts with runners

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a small tuft of silky, silver-grey, inrolled leaves, 30-40 cm tall after 18 months. It then sends stout runners over the sand that root at each node and raise leaf tufts; runners can reach 2-3 m in a season when buried by blown sand. Sexes on separate plants; females bear 20-30 cm spiky seed-head balls that roll away in the wind.
growth.source: NZ DOC Science for Conservation 122 (germination 1-3 months; 30-40 cm in 18 months; fertilised runners ~2.6 m); NZPCN spinifex guide (germination 2-6 weeks, flowers Nov-Dec, large single-sex patches, heads to 150 spikelets); ANPSA (dioecious stoloniferous perennial)

shrub.silhouette: silvery spreading crown on a short trunk

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings grow a single stout, pale stem topped by a loose rosette of large, fleshy, spoon-shaped leaves covered in silky silver hairs; after a year they are only ~35 cm tall. Branching comes later and sympodially, each shoot ending in a flat cluster of coiled white flower sprays, building the broad, rounded, silvery bush of the beach strand.
growth.source: Useful Tropical Plants (Tournefortia argentea: under 75 cm/yr, germination 2-4 weeks, seedlings ~35 cm after 12+ months, sunny sites); Hawaii-Pacific Weed Risk Assessment (4+ yr to reproduce, not shade tolerant, buoyant seeds); Plants of Hawaii; Wikipedia. H. foertherianum is a synonym. Lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Plants of Hawaii (drupe white, fleshy, globose ~4 mm, corky floating endocarp; corolla white 2.5-3.3 mm); Wikipedia (flowers ~0.6 cm); Useful Tropical Plants (flowers and fruits nearly all year; bees, butterflies). Ripening, hang and rot times, fruit set and crop estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with small oval cotyledons, then narrow, aromatic, olive-green leaves toothed near the tip and dotted with tiny amber resin glands, as in the adult. It soon branches from the base into a dense, twiggy evergreen bush; nitrogen-fixing root nodules let it grow fast (often ~1 m a year) on poor sand, and it spreads by root sprouts into thickets.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 14 m; dioecious catkins late winter-spring; waxy globular fruit in late summer-fall; birds strip the wax, needed for germination); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Myrica (small waxy dry drupes persisting over winter; no endosperm); growth and ages estimated

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (dioecious, wind-pollinated catkins late winter-spring; fruit ripe late summer-fall, globular with a pale blue-grey wax coat, used for bayberry candles); USDA Woody Plant Seed Manual Myrica (tiny dry waxy drupes that persist on the shrub over winter); set and crop estimated

growth.juvenile_note: The husked nut lies on the sand and after 2-6 months a pointed shoot pushes out of one end while the nut's flesh feeds the seedling. First leaves are entire, stiff, strap-like blades split only at the tip (bifid), in a stemless fan-like rosette; pinnate fronds come later, and a trunk rises after ~3-5 years, widening from a bulbous base ('bole').
growth.source: Wikipedia Coconut (tall palms bear at 6-10 yr, live 60-100 yr; ~11 months from female flower opening to harvest; up to 15 inflorescences/yr; ~80 nuts/yr, up to 150; nut ~1.4 kg; largely cross-pollinated, dwarfs selfing); ICRAF Agroforestree (tall selections 24-30 m, flowers after ~6th yr); germination from FAO coconut guides

fruiting.source: Wikipedia Coconut and ICRAF (new inflorescence among the leaves every ~3-4 weeks, up to 15/yr, thousands of small male flowers and ~20-50 large 25 mm female flowers per inflorescence; cross-pollinated by insects and wind; ~11-12 months to a mature brown nut that drops; 50-150 nuts per palm per year)
